message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or agree on a different target). Points come from the cards left in opponents’ hands when you finish a round. | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (red, yellow, green, blue) × 25 cards each (one 0, two 1‑9, two “Draw Two”, two “Skip”, two “Reverse”, two “Wild”, two “Wild Draw Four”). | | **Setup** | Shuffle the deck. Deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. If it’s a special card, follow its effect immediately. | | **Turn order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a “Reverse” changes direction). On your turn you may play one card that matches either color or number/symbol of the top discard, or a Wild card. If you can’t play, you must draw one card. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise the turn passes to the next player. | | **Special cards** | • **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction (in a 2‑player game it acts like Skip).
• **Wild** – You choose the new active color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – Same as Wild, but next player also draws four cards. It can only be played if you have no other playable card (otherwise you risk being challenged). | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you’re down to one card, shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player calls you out before the next turn starts, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a round** | When a player discards all their cards, they win the round. Score points: sum the values of all cards still held by opponents (number cards = face value, Draw Two/Skip/Reverse = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50). | | **Game end** | First player to reach the agreed‑upon point total wins the game. | **Optional house rules** (just pick one or mix them): | Rule | Effect | |------|--------| | **Stacking** | If a “Draw Two” or “Wild Draw Four” is played, the next player may stack another of the same type instead of drawing, passing the cumulative penalty forward. | | **No Wild Draw Four challenge** | Allow anyone to play a Wild Draw Four regardless of hand composition. | | **“Draw One” variant** | Replace “Draw Two” with “Draw One” for a gentler game. | | **“Skip” instead of “Reverse”** | In a 2‑player game, “Reverse” acts like “Skip” (no change in direction). | That’s the core of Uno! Feel free to tweak the optional rules to suit your group.
